SddRecoverFromCode.keywords: recover, from-code, restore-spec, path, brownfield, existing-scope, scope-fit, module-split, incremental, lazy, inventory-reverse, sdd-recover-from-code
SddRecoverFromCode.Mission:
Recover a spec for ONE named path — a folder or a file the operator points at — from the code that already lives there plus whatever sits next to it (README, ADR, old docs, tests). Entered from the router when the portal is LIVE and the operator both asks to recover / recreate a spec from code AND names a concrete path; the router-core beliefs it relies on are declared in `BeliefState deps` (inherited, not repeated).
Distinct from the two neighboring recovery flows: - `discover-from-code` recovers the WHOLE project's general picture and only enters from `root` when the portal is absent. This flow is the opposite scale: one path, portal already live. - `reconcile` mode=`from-code` formalizes ONE change against a spec that already exists. This flow has no existing spec for the path yet — that is exactly the gap it fills.
The agent does the reading itself — `bash` / `grep` / `Read` over the path and its neighbors — there is no dedicated recovery tool and none is being added (`AX_NO_NEW_TOOL`). It reuses the existing branches to write anything: `scope` for the scope spec, `module` for module specs, `scaffold` only if the operator wants alignment tasks. This flow owns none of that writing logic.
Input — a path (folder or file) + the operator's intent to recover its spec. Output — the path lands in a confirmed scope (existing or new) with a confirmed module split, and the module specs for it pass the same closed-world reverse check any hand-written module spec would.

BeliefState.deps: AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_TOOL_INVOCATION, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_OPERATOR_OUTPUT_LIVE_TEXT, AX_STATELESS_ARTIFACT, AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH, AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT, AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS
BeliefState.Axiom: This flow adds no CLI command and no shared-code helper. Surveying a path — what the code does, who imports whom, which docs / tests sit beside it — is done live by the agent through `bash` (`grep`, `find`, `ls`) and `Read`, the same way any engineer would open an unfamiliar folder. Building a dedicated recovery tool here trades a rare, judgment-heavy task for permanent maintenance weight — the operator has weighed that trade and rejected it. The ONLY mechanical gate in this flow is the one that already exists: `gennady lint --spec= --inventory-reverse ` (`AX_REVERSE_INVENTORY_GATE`).

Separate Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses when presenting the survey and the proposal. - **Facts** — directly read from the path: file layout, import edges, an existing test, a line in a README that states purpose. - **Assumptions** — a reasonable working read of code without a written purpose statement; mark explicitly, invite correction. - **Hypotheses** — guesses about intent that only the operator can confirm (why this exists, who else depends on it).
Conflating the three lets a guess get written into the spec as if it were read from the code — exactly the drift `--inventory-reverse` (`AX_REVERSE_INVENTORY_GATE`) later catches on the inventory side, but the vision / purpose side has no mechanical check, so hygiene here is the only guard.

Read the path incrementally, cheapest signal first, and STOP once there is enough to propose a scope fit + a module split — do not walk every file before saying anything. Cheap-to-expensive order: directory listing and file names → package / workspace manifest (if any) → README / ADR / doc files sitting beside the path → import graph of the path's own files (who it imports, who imports it) → test files (what they exercise, which is often the best behavioral evidence) → only then, if still unclear, a fuller read of the source. Present the coarse picture before going deeper; the operator can always ask for more before confirming.

A recovered module spec's Entity Inventory MUST be checked against the real code with `gennady lint --spec= --inventory-reverse ` before the flow closes. This is what separates recovering a spec from paraphrasing the code into narrative text: an inventory entry with no matching export, or an export with no inventory entry, is a finding to fix before closing — never a note for later.

Before writing any operator-facing artifact, recall the language rules — `AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE` (bureaucratic noun-for-verb phrasing, literal calque, bookish word) and `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT` (a branch name, «как обсуждали», a session-plan label) — and hold the text about to be written to them. This is the author's own pass, done in the moment of writing, not a report to the operator. The independent post-check (lint, audit) stays separate and unchanged — this pass does not replace it.

KernelGrammar.Definition:
`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE(src)` tells the agent to READ the file at `src` and apply it as part of the current task. It is a runtime lazy-load, not text to inline into any output.
- The loaded branch directive INHERITS this kernel's cross-cutting core (language, dialogue, stateless) and carries only its own deltas; it MUST NOT repeat the core. - Loading is lazy: a branch is read only when its route fires, so the kernel stays small and context is not polluted by branches that do not apply. - The reference is a file path on purpose — a directive delivered as a file keeps full instruction priority, unlike command stdout.

ChatProtocol.Contract:
Explain, then ask through the tool — a question never fires as bare free-form text. A `### 💡 <О чём решаем>` section header names the decision in plain words (no `Q` numbering, no semantic question IDs); under it, ordinary language explains the question BEFORE any tool call fires — the context, the real options, and a recommendation gated by `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (low-stakes: a direct pick is fine; high-stakes / architecture: do not pre-anchor one option — lay out the strongest candidates, a tail one included, or pair the recommendation with its strongest rival and the reason it might win instead). Only once the explanation stands does `AskUserQuestion` fire; its option list mirrors the printed order, short labels only — the argument itself lives in the message, never moved into the tool call.
Batching rule: one `AskUserQuestion` call may carry several questions ONLY when they are mutually independent — answering one does not change the meaning or the options of another (several facets of one single complex decision qualify as one batched call). Dependent questions, and any interview sequence, go one call at a time: compose the next question only after the previous answer is in.
Channel: use `AskUserQuestion` whenever the tool is available. When it is not, fall back to plain text carrying the same shape — the explanation, then an explicit list of named options the operator can answer by name — never restore `Q` labels or per-question IDs; that bare-numbered shape without the tool is itself the violation this contract forbids (`H_UNFORMATTED_ASK`).
Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (not the first typical answer):
### 💡 Формат хранения токенов Нужно решить, где держать design-токены: сгенерированный JSON проще парсить скриптам, а TS-модуль даёт автокомплит в IDE — для одного пакета без внешних потребителей разница небольшая. ✅ **JSON-файл** `[tokens.json]` — проще парсить любым языком, ничего специфичного для TS. Иначе: - **TS-модуль** `[tokens.ts]` — _за: автокомплит и типы · против: непортируемо за пределы TS_
(AskUserQuestion: «JSON-файл (рекомендую)» · «TS-модуль»)
High-stakes / architecture — do NOT pre-anchor one pick. List the strongest candidates (include a non-obvious / tail one) with «за / против» and let the operator choose; or give a recommendation only alongside its strongest alternative and the reason it might win:
### 💡 Стратегия миграции v1→v2 Три пути дают разный профиль риска и времени простоя, и откат стоит по-разному в каждом. - **Big-bang** `[migrate-all]` — _за: один переход, нет промежуточного состояния · против: долгий простой, откат дорогой_ - **Постепенная миграция по скоупам** `[migrate-incremental]` — _за: откат дешёвый, риск размазан во времени · против: два формата сосуществуют дольше_ - **Parallel-run с shadow-чтением** `[migrate-shadow]` — нетипичный вариант, но снимает риск отката почти полностью ценой временной инфраструктуры
(AskUserQuestion: «Big-bang» · «Постепенная миграция» · «Parallel-run (нетипичный)»)
A plain binary question needs no list — recommendation + inline alternative, still explained before the call:
### 💡 Нужен ли отдельный interface-скоуп Все текущие потребители — web; про API и будущих клиентов явно не говорили. ✅ **Пока не выделять** — можно добавить позже без миграции. _или сразу выделить, если API уже в планах?_
(AskUserQuestion: «Пока не выделять (рекомендую)» · «Выделить сразу»)
A counter-question in reply to a gate is a side-dive, not a rejection: (a) answer the counter-question in full, on its own merits, before returning to the gate; (b) bring the gate back exactly once, marked as a repeat pass, enriched with whatever the counter-question surfaced — «повторяю вопрос» plus a fact or option the side-dive added (e.g. operator asked "как ты делаешь ресёрч?" → the repeat pass adds an option «сначала ресёрч, потом решаем»); a verbatim repeat of the first gate carries no delta and is itself the violation. (c) if the operator answers the repeat pass with another counter-question instead of a pick, do not fire a third pass — stop and ask directly what is blocking the decision.

A halt is a plain sentence first (what happened + what to do), with the token as a trailing tag:
🛑 <что случилось по-человечески> — <что сделать оператору> `[H_*]`

SddRecoverFromCode.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_PATH_NOT_FOUND` | The named path does not exist in the repo — ask the operator for the correct one | | `H_PATH_EMPTY` | The path exists but holds no source (empty dir, docs only) — nothing to recover FROM code | | `H_NO_PORTAL` | `specs/README.md` is absent — this is project-scale recovery, not one-path recovery; redirect to `ai/directives/sdd-v2/root.directive.xml` (which enters `discover-from-code` on an empty portal) | | `H_SCOPE_NOT_CONFIRMED` | Operator rejects or leaves open the proposed scope fit / scope-type / module split — stop; nothing is written |

Step.Goal: Validate the path and the portal before spending any read.
Step.Action: Confirm the named path exists and contains source (`H_PATH_NOT_FOUND` / `H_PATH_EMPTY` otherwise). Confirm the portal is live (`specs/README.md` present — `H_NO_PORTAL` otherwise, which hands off to project-scale recovery instead). Both gates are cheap and mechanical; clear them before STEP_1.

Step.Goal: Read the path and its neighbors — dosed, not exhaustive (`AX_DOSED_SURVEY`).
Step.Action: Walk the cheap-to-expensive order from `AX_DOSED_SURVEY`: layout → manifest → README / ADR / docs beside the path → import edges in and out → tests → deeper source read only if still unclear. Keep Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses apart throughout (`AX_EVIDENCE_HYGIENE`). Also read the current portal's Scope Graph + Scopes table (`sdd-state`) — the survey needs the existing scopes to judge fit against.

Step.Goal: Propose scope fit, scope-type, and a module split; let the operator steer.
Step.Action: Present the survey plain Russian, coarse first (`AX_EVIDENCE_HYGIENE` tri-split, confidence marked per item): what the path does, which existing scope it fits OR that a new scope is needed, the scope-type if new, and a first-cut module split. Where the fit or the split is a genuine fork (new scope vs. folding into an existing one; where the module boundary falls) — run it through `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/interview-protocol.directive.xml")` so each fork gets its own question, one at a time, rather than a single multi-part ask. Outright rejection or an unresolved fork → `H_SCOPE_NOT_CONFIRMED`. STOP.

Step.Goal: Write the spec by reusing the existing authoring branches — no bespoke writing logic here.
Step.Action: Before handing off, run the self-check pass per `AX_ARTIFACT_STYLE_SELF_CHECK` on any text this flow writes itself (the survey, the proposal); each branch called below carries its own copy of the same gate for the artifact it writes. On confirmation, hand off to the branches that already know how to write a spec, in dependency order: - `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/scope.directive.xml")` — create the new scope spec, or extend the existing one the path was folded into. - `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/module.directive.xml")` — write the module spec(s) for the confirmed split, entity inventory sourced from what STEP_1 actually read. - Optionally, if the operator wants the code brought in line with anything the recovery surfaced (missing tests, a contract gap): `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/scaffold.directive.xml")`. This flow contributes none of the spec-writing rules — it only routes the confirmed picture into the branch that owns each artifact.

Step.Goal: Prove the recovered spec matches the real code, not a paraphrase of it.
Step.Action: For every module spec produced: `gennady lint --spec= --inventory-reverse ` clean (`AX_REVERSE_INVENTORY_GATE`) — fix the inventory or the spec, not the code, when it disagrees with reality. Then `sdd-check --all .` clean over the whole tree. Return control.

SddRecoverFromCode.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, never narrated (`AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `🧭 RFC_R · path= · scope= · step=`.
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch)
`` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`, its OWN paragraph (a blank line above it, not just a `\n`) — markdown collapses a single newline into a space, so without the blank line the breadcrumb visually fuses onto the service line
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — per `UNDERSTANDING_BLOCK_FORMAT` (goes at the TOP) ### 🎯 Главное решение — the crux in plain words; add a diagram per `FLOW_DIAGRAM_WHEN` if it is a flow ### 💡 <О чём решаем> — per `QUESTION_FORMAT` ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
Glyph dictionary — closed inventory, one assigned meaning each, never a free pick. Every glyph here is chosen to read clearly on BOTH a light and a dark terminal/chat theme — half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓` and similar) are forbidden anywhere in this layout: they render as near-invisible or vanish outright depending on theme.
Section-header glyphs (fixed, one per header, in the order above): - `🤔` — the agent's own understanding check, at the top of a decision card - `🎯` — the crux decision, in plain words - `💡` — a decision the agent is proposing for the operator to confirm or pick between - `↓` — folded detail, expand on demand
Step-TYPE glyphs (fixed, keyed by the step's TYPE, used in the service line / breadcrumb, never a free pick): - `🏗` — creation / scaffold (new spec, new tickets, new files) - `🔍` — audit / review (fresh-eyes read, no write) - `🔧` — fix / reconcile (spec ⟷ code drift repair) - `⚡` — execute (a task ticket's phases running) - `🗺` — routing / overview (intent classification, project-level map)
Breadcrumb-status glyphs (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): `✅` done · `👷` active · `◻️` not yet.
No other emoji appear in message or section headers — the glyphs enumerated above are the only ones this layout permits.
Decision first, reasoning on demand. The must-read top of a message is short: where we are + my read + what to decide. Everything heavy — full option comparison, evidence, the change-list, derivations — goes BELOW a `### ↓ Детали — по желанию` header. Never dump reasoning above the questions. Facts already verified collapse to one line («сверился: …»); uncertainties that need the operator BECOME the questions — never list them twice.
